item.title: Tart Cherry
item.description:
What it is: Tart cherry is a fruit extract rich in anthocyanins—powerful antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds that improve sleep quality, reduce muscle soreness, and support recovery. Clinical research shows it works comparably to some sleep medications without side effects, making it one of the most evidence-backed natural sleep aids available.

What Is Tart Cherry?

Tart cherry (Prunus cerasus) is a sour cherry variety grown primarily in North America, distinct from sweet cherries commonly eaten fresh. While tart cherries are too sour for fresh consumption, they’re ideal for juices, concentrates, and supplements—forms that concentrate their bioactive compounds.

item.title: MSM (Methylsulfonylmethane)
item.description:
What Is MSM?

Methylsulfonylmethane (MSM) is an organic sulfur compound found naturally in plants, animals, and humans. It provides bioavailable sulfur, the fourth most abundant mineral in the human body and an essential building block for numerous biological processes.

MSM occurs naturally in foods like vegetables, fruits, grains, and animal products, but in relatively small amounts. Supplemental MSM provides concentrated sulfur that supports joint health, reduces inflammation, and promotes healthy skin, hair, and nails. It has been used for decades as a natural approach to joint discomfort and inflammatory conditions.

item.title: Astaxanthin
item.description:
What Is Astaxanthin?

Astaxanthin is a xanthophyll carotenoid, a lipid-soluble pigment produced by the microalga Haematococcus pluvialis as a stress response mechanism. This compound is responsible for the red coloration in salmon, shrimp, and krill. Unlike other carotenoids, astaxanthin possesses a unique molecular structure featuring ionone rings at both ends with a conjugated polyene chain, allowing it to embed itself across the entire thickness of the cell membrane.
